18	The Defendants contend that the Complaint should be dismissed in its entirety for failure to comply with the 2004 Agreement’s dispute resolution and mediation clause. L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. The clause provides that “[a]ny dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof shall first be referred by the parties to their senior-level executives for attempted resolution through good-faith negotiations.” Compl. Ex. A § 9.1 (emphasis added). Should negotiations fail, thirty days after making a written request to initiate those negotiations, “either Party may, by written notice to the other, require that the Dispute be referred to non-binding mediation administered by the American Arbitration Association.” Id. (emphasis added). The Defendants assert that Skold did not refer a dispute to a senior-level executive for negotiations and failed to make a written request that the dispute be referred to nonbinding mediation. L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. Skold responds that the language of the mediation clause is permissive (“either Party may ... require”) and also argues that, in any event, Inc. has waived its right to invoke the clause because it participated in litigation over the dispute in the cancellation action before the TTAB. See Pl.’s L.P./Inc. Opp’n at 14-15.
19	The dispute resolution clause in the 2004 Agreement contains two clauses, one of which is mandatory (the parties shall refer the matter to senior executives to attempt to negotiate a resolution) and the other which is permissive (the parties may refer the matter to nonbinding mediation). Given the voluntary nature of the latter, this Court agrees with Skold that he was not required to refer this dispute to mediation before bringing suit here against Inc.
20	L.P. and S.A., who are not parties to the 2004 Agreement, also contend that the dispute resolution clause requires their dismissal from this action. In essence, they urge this Court to accept the contention that a nonparty to an agreement should be permitted to force a signatory party to engage in negotiations pursuant to a permissive mediation clause in that agreement as a condition precedent to filing suit but cite no relevant case or statute in support of this contention. See United States v. Benish, 5 F.3d 20, 26 (3d Cir.1993) (rejecting a party’s claim where the party “provided] no legal support for his argument or any persuasive reason” for the court to find in his favor). The Court sees no persuasive reason to dismiss Skold’s entire Complaint based on this unsupported argument. Accordingly, the motion to dismiss the Complaint against L.P. and S.A. on this ground shall be denied.
21	Regarding Inc.: although Skold did fail to bring in a senior-level executive to try to resolve the dispute — as he was required to do under the dispute resolution provision — Inc.’s participation in the TTAB proceedings waived any rights it may have had to seek to have the parties’ executives negotiate an end to the dispute. See, e.g., LBL Skysystems (USA), Inc. v. APG-Am., Inc., No. 02-5379, 2005 WL 2140240, at *30 (E.D.Pa. Aug. 31, 2005) (holding that a “party that engages in discovery and files pretrial motions waives a contract’s alternative dispute resolution provision”); Smith v. IMG Worldwide, Inc., 360 F.Supp.2d 681, 687 (E.D.Pa.2005) (finding that a party’s engaging in motion practice and providing “substantial discovery” constituted waiver of contractual alternative dispute resolution provision).
22	Viewing the four years’ worth of docket entries in the TTAB action, the Court considers that Inc. did not file a motion to stay the TTAB proceedings pending executive-level negotiations and instead filed, inter alia, motions to dismiss, a protective order, multiple summary judgment motions (one of which was partially granted in its favor), and a final brief in preparation for trial. See, e.g., Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897, 2012 WL 5902083 (T.T.A.B. Nov. 8, 2012) (granting Inc.’s motion for partial summary judgment on Skold’s abandonment claim). See also generally Registrant’s Trial Brief, Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897 (T.T.A.B. Aug. 13, 2014), Docket No. 81. This four-year history of litigation in the cancellation action — from filing nearly through trial — is, on its face, inconsistent with the notion that Inc. was willing to engage in the good-faith executive-level negotiations required by the dispute resolution provision.
23	Moreover, the Court can look to the TTAB’s grant of partial summary judgment in favor of Inc. and dismissing Skold’s abandonment claim as a concrete example of an instance where Inc.’s conduct inconsistent with the dispute resolution clause caused prejudice to Skold, not to mention the expenditure of time, cost, and resources attendant to maintaining a multi-year trademark cancellation action. The Defendants have undisputedly accepted the judicial process and have demonstrated that fact by: (1) Inc.’s failure to raise the issue of good-faith negotiations promptly before the TTAB; (2) Inc.’s engaging in discovery in the TTAB action; (3) Inc.’s filing of several pretrial motions in the TTAB action, none of which raise the issue of negotiation; and (4) the Defendants’ decision to wait until the case was ready to proceed to trial before the TTAB and until a Complaint was filed in this Court before asserting Skold’s failure to negotiate as grounds for a motion to dismiss. See St. Clair Area Sch. Dist. Bd. of Educ. v. E.I. Assocs., 733 A.2d 677, 682 n. 6 (Pa.Commw.Ct.1999) (“The key to determining whether [an alternative dispute resolution procedure] has been waived is whether the party, by virtue of its conduct, has accepted the judicial process.”). Inc. cannot now attempt to stand on the alternative dispute resolution clause as a reason for dismissal. Its right to invoke the clause has been waived.
24	```

1	# Worked example — Category 1.3 — general-vs-specific / list scope
2	
3	Contract `93FSupp3d375_personal_deposit_account_agreement`, filed in 93 F.Supp.3d 375.
4	
5	A court construed **4** of this contract's provisions; the other **251** it did not. Read that as the base rate to expect, NOT as a quota to reproduce.
6	
7	## HIGH RISK — a federal court construed this provision
8	
9	"Part I — International ACH and Wire Transactions (NACHA Operating Rules)"  (risk type: 1.3)
10	
11	```
12	International ACH and Wire Transactions If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved, and the laws enforced by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”). Under such rules and laws, we may temporarily suspend processing of a transaction for greater scrutiny or verification against the OFAC list of blocked parties, which may result in delayed settlement, posting and/or availability of funds. If we determine there is a violation, or if we cannot satisfactorily resolve a suspected or potential violation, the subject funds will be blocked as required by law. If you believe you have adequate grounds to seek the return of any blocked funds, it is your sole responsibility to pursue the matter with the appropriate governmental authorities. Please see the OFAC website for procedures and form required to seek a release of blocked funds.
13	```
14	
15	### What the court said, verbatim from the opinion in 93 F.Supp.3d 375
16	
17	```
18	The bulk of Plaintiffs’ breach claim centers around their argument that TD’s conduct violated the NACHA Rules, which Plaintiffs claim were incorporated into the Account Agreement. See Compl. at ¶ 166-67. In order to address this claim we must first determine whether the NACHA rules were in fact incorporated. In support of this point, Plaintiffs cite to page 16 of the Account Agreement, which states in relevant part:
19	International ACH and Wire Transactions
20	If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved....
21	As TD points out, this provision does not refer to all ACH transactions, but rather only to those initiated from outside of the United States. Motion to Dismiss at 18 (Doc. No. 23). Thus to the extent that an ACH transaction was initiated within the United States, we see nothing in the Account Agreement that would obligate TD to follow the NACHA rules for processing that transaction.
22	TD argues further that Plaintiffs “have not alleged that any of the ACH debits at issue were initiated outside of the United States,” Doc. Again, the touchstone is plausibility. Ethypharm, 707 F.3d at 231 n. 14. Taking the Plaintiffs’ allegations as true, the Complaint raises a plausible claim that some number of the loans originated outside of the United States. The Account Agreement provides that the parties must abide by the NACHA rules for the processing of those transactions.

SECTION 10

Half-Day Boys

10-A. In accordance with and subject to the
provisions herein contained, half-day boys may be
employed who are not members of the Union upon
such terms as may be agreed upon between such
boys and the Publishers,

10-B. A “half-day boy” means an employee of
the Fublisher working within the hours herein-
after specified in aid of and under the direction
of a route man.

10-C, No Publisher of a morning newspaper
may employ any half-day boys.

10-D. Publishers of afternoon papers may em-
ploy half-day boys to work only between the hours
of three o'clock and eight o’clock jin the after-
noon, except on Saturdays when they may begin
at 12:00 o’clock noon. ' ‘

10-E. No half-day boy may be employed to
draw newspapers directly from a Publisher's
plant.

10-F. Publishers employing half-day boys shall
prepare a list of all such boys now in their em-
ploy and the particular routes or points at which
they are employed, and shall furnish copies of
such lists together with written notice of all sub-
sequent changes therein to the Joint Standing
Committee and/or Appeals Board, the Publishers’
Association, and the Union.

10-G. Except as hereinafter provided, each Pub-
lisher shall be limited to the number of half-day
boys now employed by him, nor shall he increase
such number, nor shall he increase the number
of half-day boys now employed by him on any
given route or at any given point, nor shall he
employ any half-day boys on a route or at any
given point on which none is being employed at
this time,

10-H. In the event of the discontinuance of a
route on which a half-day boy or boys are now
employed, such boy or boys shall be eliminated,
and the positions so vacated shall not be filled, and
the total number of half-day boys permitted to
such Publisher shall be reduced accordingly.

10-I, In the event of the merger or consolida-
tion of routes on any of which a half-day boy

10-J. In the event a Publisher who is permitted

18-A. 4. Cost of Living Allowance: On each

anniversary date of the contract, March 81, 1982,

and March 31, 1983, employees covered hereunder
shall receive a cost of living adjustment to the
scheduled wage increases in accordance with the
following formula:

The Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price
Index (C.P.1.-W; 1967=100) for New York City,
hereafter called the Index, shali be used for all
measurements of the change in cost of living.

Effective March 831, 1982, the amount of any
cost of living adjustment shall be the percentage
increase in excess of 6% in the Index for May
1982 over May 1981 (as reported in June each
year) multipled by the day scales and the result-
ant amount shall be added to the day scales.

Effective March 31, 1988, the amount of any
cost of living adjustment shall be the percentage
increase in excess of 6¢¢ in the Index for May

The Times and the Union agree as set forth
below on certain aspeets of The Times’ opera-
tions at its new facility at Carlstadt, New Jersey.

Two major factors in the decision of The
Times to make the large capital investment re-

. Gaired by the Carlstadt facility were the need

‘go make substantial productivity gains and to
meet the competitive challenge of suburban news-
papers. The partics recognize that the challenge
of suburban newspapers can be met only if the
production and distribution of The Times are
timely and meet the needs of the reader.
Accordingly, The Times and the Union commit
themselves to-the achievement of maximum pro-
ductivity and efficiency at the Carlstadt facility
consistent with the terms of this memorandum
and of the contract. This does not preclude the
Union from negotiating for manning that is
hecessary to perform the various tasks in its
jurisdiction and to avoid undue hardships.

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c001","reasoning_cat1":"A gender-neutral reading convention using ordinary language ('may connote a masculine gender ... intended to include all employees'); nothing here has two competing operative meanings.","reasoning_cat2":"It is an interpretive aid that harmonises with every substantive provision (e.g. 2-A.1's 'Route men', 4-A.3's 'No man'); no operative term contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c002","reasoning_cat1":"'as agent of the following individual Publishers' and 'binding upon each of the said individual Publishers or its successor' leaves 'successor' wholly undefined, a term with real reach in a multiemployer setting.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits against Section 19, which says the Agreement 'was negotiated individually ... and shall be treated ... as an individual agreement,' creating a genuine question whether this is one association-wide contract or two.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c003","reasoning_cat1":"The boundary is fixed only 'approximately' — 'a radius of approximately fifty miles' and 'bounded approximately as follows' — so the outer edge of the Metropolitan Area cannot be applied with precision.","reasoning_cat2":"'Metropolitan Area' is load-bearing throughout (2-E.1, 2-E.2(e), 3-E, 12-A.1, 21-D V), and the Carlstadt/Newspoint and over-the-road provisions depend on where the line falls.","prob_cat1":0.41,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c004","reasoning_cat1":"A long enumerated list of covered operations with an internal exception ('Collectors, except in the case of any Publisher using a billing system operated through the auditing department') invites expressio unius arguments about work not named.","reasoning_cat2":"2-B immediately adds a catch-all for 'any other operation,' and 2-C, 2-H.2 and the Carlstadt jurisdiction minutes all pull on the same unit boundary.","prob_cat1":0.38,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c005","reasoning_cat1":"The definition of 'dealer' is introduced by 'i.e.' but gives only an example, and the text is broken ('or in the same manner as present practice'), leaving the exception's scope unclear.","reasoning_cat2":"Its 'no regular situation holder ... shall be laid off solely as a result' tracks 2-E.2(i) and 3-D.4 but sits against the broad layoff right in 3-D.1.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c006","reasoning_cat1":"This is the paradigm general catch-all after an enumerated list: 'any other operation, occupation or branch of work which is now being performed exclusively by employees for whom the Union is now the recognized bargaining representative' — 'exclusively' and 'now' both bite.","reasoning_cat2":"Read with 2-A.1's specific list and 2-H.1's preservation of other unions' mailroom jurisdiction, the reach of the catch-all is genuinely contestable.","prob_cat1":0.46,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c007","reasoning_cat1":"'new mechanical devices ... to perform or aid in the performance of any of the operations included in the bargaining unit' is broad but its terms are ordinary; 'aid in' is the soft spot.","reasoning_cat2":"It pushes against 3-D.4/3-D.5, which contemplate automated systems creating excess situations, and against 2-H.1's preservation of other unions' jurisdiction.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c008","reasoning_cat1":"A flat recognition of named terminals as delivery points; no term carries two meanings.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 2-E.1 and 2-E.2; nothing in the instrument contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c009","reasoning_cat1":"'to areas where for any reason distribution is interrupted' is open-ended, though the operative grant is a simple permission.","reasoning_cat2":"Fits with 2-A.1's 'Canada men' and 3-C; no competing provision found.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c010","reasoning_cat1":"The final saving clause ('this shall not be deemed to curtail the right to make substitution for a bus or railroad now being used') cuts against the prohibition just stated, and 'existing means or methods' is undefined.","reasoning_cat2":"2-E.2(h) lets a Publisher 'at any time increase, decrease, or discontinue any over-the-road trucking and employ railroad, aircraft, or any other form of transportation,' which is hard to square with the approval requirement here.","prob_cat1":0.38,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c011","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence of plain permission that employees 'may be required to operate tractor-trailer trucks.'","reasoning_cat2":"It is the gateway to the rest of 2-E.2 and to 22-D's Times-specific gloss, but standing alone it is consistent with them.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c012","reasoning_cat1":"'who are qualified, in order of seniority' could mean qualified-then-seniority or seniority-among-qualified, a small but real ambiguity.","reasoning_cat2":"It cross-refers to Section 4-B, which governs bidding for vacant situations rather than selection of drivers, so the cited mechanism does not obviously fit.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c013","reasoning_cat1":"'A reasonable number of employees' is a vague quantity with no boundary supplied anywhere.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision defines or caps training opportunities; it sits comfortably beside 2-E.2(b).","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c014","reasoning_cat1":"'This article is intended only to establish terms and conditions for operating tractor-trailer trucks' is a scope-limiting sentence that fights with the broad grant in the same paragraph.","reasoning_cat2":"'The Publishers shall be free to select any runs' is in tension with 2-E.2(e)'s requirement that transfer points be 'agreed upon by the parties' and with 3-E's methods-and-extent freeze.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c015","reasoning_cat1":"'as near the limits of such areas as practical' is a vague standard, and the carve-out for runs 'specifically dealt with in (e)(1)' must be read against it.","reasoning_cat2":"22-D Point Two expressly directs that paragraph (e) 'will be construed as if it reads as follows' for The Times, substituting a 250-mile/two-stop regime — a direct textual override.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.46},
{"clause_id":"c016","reasoning_cat1":"'Albany or any other city designated by the Publisher outside the Metropolitan Area' is broad but operationally clear.","reasoning_cat2":"22-D(i) excepts common-carrier runs beyond 250 miles or with more than two stops, which qualifies this through-driving rule for The Times.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c017","reasoning_cat1":"OCR damage aside, the mechanics ('presently recognized exchange points at or near the city line') are concrete.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 2-E.2(g) and 3-E; no contradicting term located.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c018","reasoning_cat1":"A short conditional permission; 'jurisdictional dispute with another union' is a recognised term of art here.","reasoning_cat2":"It parallels 2-H.1 and 9-B's jurisdictional-conflict carve-outs, and 22-D(vii) uses the same escape; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c019","reasoning_cat1":"'to the extent that such forms of transportation may now be employed' is an undefined baseline qualifying an otherwise unlimited management right.","reasoning_cat2":"22-D Point (x) expressly stipulates that '(h) may not be invoked by The Times' to reassign nine-month runs to a common carrier, and 3-E freezes methods and extent — both cut against it.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.45},
{"clause_id":"c020","reasoning_cat1":"'laid off solely as a result of the establishment of the run' turns entirely on 'solely,' a qualifier that routinely generates causation disputes.","reasoning_cat2":"It must be reconciled with 3-D.1's recognised right to lay off 'for economic or business reasons' and 3-D.2's expansive definition of those reasons.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c021","reasoning_cat1":"A fixed dollar bonus tied to a defined triggering event; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Parallel in form to 3-Q's hi-lo bonus and consistent with the wage schedules in 13-A.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c022","reasoning_cat1":"A narrow prohibition on contracting with another union as to inspectors and Return Department employees; terms are specific.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits beside 2-H.1's preservation of other unions' mailroom jurisdiction but does not contradict it.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c023","reasoning_cat1":"The tail 'present practice, however, excepted' swallows the rule without identifying what the practice is.","reasoning_cat2":"Similar 'present practice' savings appear in 3-G, 12-C and 5-N, so the pattern is consistent even if individually vague.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c024","reasoning_cat1":"'Conditions and methods of operation now prevailing ... shall not be disturbed' freezes an unspecified baseline, and the arbitration duty is conditioned on 'provided such other union or unions agree.'","reasoning_cat2":"It overlaps 16-M.3's no-change-in-condition rule and cuts against the management rights in 3-B, 3-D.1 and 3-I.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c025","reasoning_cat1":"'When full operations commence at an annex or a new or additional building' leaves 'full operations' undefined for a jurisdiction trigger.","reasoning_cat2":"It cross-refers to 2-A and 2-B, and the Carlstadt (22-A) and Newspoint (21-D) jurisdiction memoranda set out different, plant-specific allocations.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c026","reasoning_cat1":"A clear reciprocal rule about assignment and inability to perform other operations; the double negative is awkward but not ambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4-A.4 (competence) and 14-B (physical incapacity); no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c027","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence is broken — 'shall be entitled to for work' is missing its verb (evidently 'to shape') — so the right created cannot be read off the text.","reasoning_cat2":"The default/restitution rule fits 2-A.1's 'Collectors' and 13-F/13-G on collections and shortages; no contradiction found.","prob_cat1":0.44,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c028","reasoning_cat1":"A clean prohibition with a stated exception for foremen and assistant foremen.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 10 permits non-member 'half-day boys' to work 'in aid of and under the direction of a route man,' which sits awkwardly against this bar on non-covered employees performing Section 2 operations.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c029","reasoning_cat1":"'maximum Union security permissible under the Labor Management Relations Act ... to the extent embodied in Section 17' defines the obligation only by reference, so its content is uncertain on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 17-A.1 says the closed-shop language is reprinted 'for reference only and not as a part of this Agreement,' while 17-A.2 revives it automatically if law permits — a genuine tension with a clause that measures union security by Section 17.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c030","reasoning_cat1":"A definite 30-day membership rule tied to regular situation holder status.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 2-N.3's agency-fee mechanism for non-members and with 2-L.1; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c031","reasoning_cat1":"The heading is 'Work on Sixth Shift' but the text addresses competence and the fifth shift, and the first sentence is corrupt ('employed to an the requirements'); the meaning cannot be read straight off it.","reasoning_cat2":"Nearly identical language appears in the italicised former 2-L reprinted in 17-A.1, which is declared 'not a part of this Agreement,' so the same words appear twice with opposite operative status.","prob_cat1":0.44,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c032","reasoning_cat1":"One short flat prohibition; 'engage any person to aid him' is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 10-B defines half-day boys as working 'in aid of and under the direction of a route man,' which requires reconciling but is employer-engaged rather than employee-engaged.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c033","reasoning_cat1":"A detailed, mechanical check-off procedure with fixed timing; nothing genuinely two-sided.","reasoning_cat2":"The October 26, 1981 letter agrees 'to amend section 2-N.1 to provide for the checkoff of dues on a weekly or bi-weekly basis,' which supersedes the monthly mechanics on notice.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c034","reasoning_cat1":"A statutory-compliance sentence with no operative discretion.","reasoning_cat2":"Mirrors 17-B's separability approach; no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c035","reasoning_cat1":"The cap — 'the amount payable per shift' shall not 'exceed 5% of the monthly dues payable by regular situation holders' — mixes per-shift and monthly measures, which can be read more than one way.","reasoning_cat2":"It applies to 'non-member extras and casuals' while 2-L.2 requires membership only of regular situation holders; the two fit together.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c036","reasoning_cat1":"'the schedules shown in the last notice of such schedules to the Union' incorporates an unidentified external document, though the 46-pound cap is precise.","reasoning_cat2":"22-H prescribes Times bundle schedules including 'bundle weight of 42 pounds or more' and 37-46 pound loadings, which must be squared with the frozen schedules and the 46-pound ceiling.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c037","reasoning_cat1":"A duty to publish a schedule; the content criteria are left open but the obligation is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Newspoint (21-D I) and 21-C.2 set specific load maxima that operate alongside these plant schedules.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c038","reasoning_cat1":"A simple posting and furnishing duty.","reasoning_cat2":"Parallels 4-G's list-posting duty; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c039","reasoning_cat1":"'unduly burdensome' is a vague standard with no metric, and the Publisher's counterpart trigger is the equally open 'newspaper operational conditions warrant it.'","reasoning_cat2":"It routes to Section 16, consistent with the rest of the grievance architecture.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c040","reasoning_cat1":"'unduly burdensome' and 'unduly difficult to serve' are undefined standards limiting an otherwise absolute management right.","reasoning_cat2":"16-M.3 forbids any 'change in condition' without the other party's prior consent, which is hard to reconcile with an unqualified right to determine wrapping, receipt points and dealer counts.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c041","reasoning_cat1":"'shall at their respective points personally supply all dealers and newsboys' is short and definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 2-D.2's Canada points; nothing contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c042","reasoning_cat1":"'as such Publisher may find necessary or desirable' is a subjective standard, and review is limited to whether the layoff 'was for economic or business reasons.'","reasoning_cat2":"It collides with 3-D.4's flat ban on automation layoffs of listed holders, 2-E.2(i), 2-A.2 and 20-E.6's express waiver of layoff rights on the Bulldog phase-out.","prob_cat1":0.25,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c043","reasoning_cat1":"A definitional clause that both invokes 'usual and ordinary sense' and sweeps in 'all reasons of an economic or business character' — self-referential and boundaryless.","reasoning_cat2":"It is drafted precisely to control 3-D.1, and no other provision cuts across it except the automation carve-out in 3-D.4.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c044","reasoning_cat1":"The provision requires employment of laid-off wholesaler employees while saying it 'shall in no way limit the Publisher's right to lay off pursuant to Section 3-D' — an internal pull that only the 15-day delay resolves.","reasoning_cat2":"It cross-refers generally to 'Section 3-D' and to the methods-and-extent rules in 3-E/3-F, and 12-D.1 provides a separate financial-benefits regime for the same laid-off wholesaler employees.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c045","reasoning_cat1":"'Such automated process or automated system shall be construed to include, among other such ... conveyor belts, wire-tying machines and the like' is a classic ejusdem generis list, and the 1981 list/1965 date pairing is odd.","reasoning_cat2":"The absolute no-layoff promise is difficult to reconcile with 3-D.1's recognised layoff right and 3-D.6's savings language.","prob_cat1":0.37,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c046","reasoning_cat1":"Long and intricate but each step (declaration of excess, bidding under 4-B, assignment of starting time and days off) is specified.","reasoning_cat2":"The mechanism parallels 20-E.5's 'excess situation holder' regime for the Bulldog phase-out, which uses a different placement rule.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c047","reasoning_cat1":"A stacked savings clause — 'as many regular situations as possible, subject to the terms of Sections 3-D.1 and 16 ... and other pertinent provisions thereof' — that preserves obligations while subordinating them to their own opposite.","reasoning_cat2":"It expressly points at 5-G and 3-D.1, two provisions that pull in opposite directions, so harmonising them is exactly the exercise it invites.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c048","reasoning_cat1":"'Methods and extent of direct delivery and combined delivery ... as they exist ... at the time of the effective date hereof are to be continued' freezes an undefined status quo and does not say what counts as a 'change.'","reasoning_cat2":"3-F gives the Publisher free choice on new routes, 2-E.2(h) lets it discontinue over-the-road trucking at will, and a side letter 'Clarification of Method and Extent' says the agreement 'prohibits the subcontracting of bargaining unit deliveries except as it may exist pursuant to the contract.'","prob_cat1":0.42,"prob_cat2":0.50},
{"clause_id":"c049","reasoning_cat1":"'new sections or new routes' is the whole battleground and is left undefined against existing routes.","reasoning_cat2":"It is the direct counterweight to 3-E's freeze, and the two together determine when Joint Standing Committee approval is needed.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.43},
{"clause_id":"c050","reasoning_cat1":"'Present practices' are frozen without identification, and 'good cause shown' is an open standard.","reasoning_cat2":"12-C repeats this paragraph essentially verbatim, so the same rule appears twice in the instrument — redundancy that invites argument about whether they mean the same thing.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c051","reasoning_cat1":"'undue hardship or hazard,' 'excessive work tasks' and 'insofar as practicable' are three undefined standards in one paragraph.","reasoning_cat2":"The News side letter on 'Heaters, Bostrum Seats and Safety Equipment' adds equipment commitments that overlay the heater/defroster duty here.","prob_cat1":0.40,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c052","reasoning_cat1":"'coverage in the amount of $20,000, $50,000 beginning January 1, 1982' is punctuated so badly that the operative amounts and dates must be inferred, and the trigger ('assaults or other criminal conduct') is a general catch-all after a specific.","reasoning_cat2":"Coverage overlaps the Welfare Fund (13-H) and the Times/News life insurance provisions (22-G), but no direct contradiction appears.","prob_cat1":0.46,"prob_cat2":0.14},

{"clause_id":"c100","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence premium rule with a fixed window and rate.","reasoning_cat2":"5-I sets double time for advance-section work in exactly the same Sunday 10:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. window, and 5-H sets double time for certain Sunday evening-paper work.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.39},
{"clause_id":"c101","reasoning_cat1":"'sufficiently far from where it began to involve substantial travel time' is doubly vague, and the clause then defers the whole arrangement to future negotiation.","reasoning_cat2":"It routes failure to agree to the Joint Standing Committee, consistent with Section 16; no contradicting provision found.","prob_cat1":0.43,"prob_cat2":0.16},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c113","reasoning_cat1":"'from the beginning of the night shift on the night before the holiday to the end of the day shift of the holiday itself' is a workable but unusual span definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Because 5-B's night shift runs to 10:00 a.m. and 5-A's day shift to 8:00 p.m., the holiday span overlaps two calendar days and must be reconciled with 7-C and 7-E.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c114","reasoning_cat1":"'thereafter price and one-half of the holiday rate' is a plain misprint for 'time and one-half,' and the two-days'-pay floor plus premium structure is hard to read as written.","reasoning_cat2":"It cross-refers to 'sick leave as defined in Section 18-B. 2.' when the sick-leave definition is in 13-B.2, and 7-E sets a different (double-rate) formula for holiday work at a non-issuing Publisher.","prob_cat1":0.42,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c115","reasoning_cat1":"The qualifying test ('at least four (4) days' work ... during each of the three (3) payroll weeks immediately preceding ... and during such week as well') is arithmetically precise.","reasoning_cat2":"20-D applies this test to Group 1 men on vacation while directing payment 'in accordance with Section 13-B. 4,' knitting three provisions together in a way that needs reconciling.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c116","reasoning_cat1":"'double the regular and overtime rates' is a clear formula on its own.","reasoning_cat2":"7-C prescribes 'not less than two (2) days' pay for the regular shift worked and thereafter [time] and one-half of the holiday rate' for the same act of working a holiday, so the two premium formulas overlap.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.37},
{"clause_id":"c117","reasoning_cat1":"An anti-offset rule stated plainly with defined statutory references.","reasoning_cat2":"It parallels 22-F and 22-G's anti-reduction promises; no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c118","reasoning_cat1":"'provided these activities do not interfere with the performance of their duties' is a vague proviso, though the following sentence narrows it.","reasoning_cat2":"8-C reinforces the same protection for overtime distribution; no contrary provision found.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c119","reasoning_cat1":"The 48-hour overtime production duty and the three-week look-back are precise, though the unrelated final sentence about chapel meetings sits oddly.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 20-F's paycheck-error correction and 5-J's list of starting times; no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c120","reasoning_cat1":"'will not be discriminated against insofar as the distribution of overtime' is grammatically incomplete but its sense is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"It qualifies 5-M's employer control over overtime distribution without contradicting it.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c121","reasoning_cat1":"A mandatory routing rule ('shall be delivered in bulk from the place of printing to the plant or plants operated by the Publisher') whose scope turns on 'not owned or controlled,' an undefined test.","reasoning_cat2":"9-B softens the same subject to an 'endeavor' qualified by cost and jurisdictional escape, and the Lancaster side letter treats outside-plant transport as still to be negotiated.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c122","reasoning_cat1":"'shall endeavor' plus 'providing doing so does not involve the Publisher in increased cost or a jurisdictional conflict' makes the obligation nearly self-cancelling and supplies no cost benchmark.","reasoning_cat2":"9-A states the delivery requirement in mandatory terms for the same category of outside-printed sections, so the two paragraphs impose different levels of obligation.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c123","reasoning_cat1":"'upon such terms as may be agreed upon between such boys and the Publishers' leaves the entire employment relationship outside the Agreement's terms.","reasoning_cat2":"2-A.1 recognises the Union as exclusive representative for the listed operations and 2-K bars non-covered employees from performing them, which is difficult to square with individually negotiated non-member helpers.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c124","reasoning_cat1":"'working within the hours hereinafter specified in aid of and under the direction of a route man' is a definition that depends entirely on 10-D.","reasoning_cat2":"2-M says 'No employee shall engage any person to aid him in the performance of the work assigned to him,' which reads awkwardly against a category defined as aiding a routeman.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c125","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line categorical prohibition.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 10-D's limitation to afternoon papers.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c126","reasoning_cat1":"'between the hours of three o'clock and eight o'clock in the afternoon' is loosely expressed (eight o'clock is not afternoon) but the intended window is evident.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 10-C and 10-B's 'hours hereinafter specified.'","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c127","reasoning_cat1":"A short flat prohibition.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 10-B's role definition; nothing contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c128","reasoning_cat1":"'all such boys now in their employ' fixes a baseline at an unstated date in a document reprinting decades-old text.","reasoning_cat2":"The freeze depends on the same 'now' used in 10-G and 10-H, so the whole Section 10 baseline is undated together.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c129","reasoning_cat1":"'the number ... now employed by him' and 'on which none is being employed at this time' freeze an unidentified historical baseline, and the sentence stacks four negatives.","reasoning_cat2":"10-J allows an increase 'even though it may thereby increase the total number,' an express exception to this cap.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c130","reasoning_cat1":"A clear attrition rule tied to a defined event.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 10-G's cap and 10-I's merger rule.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c131","reasoning_cat1":"An agreement to negotiate with a specified fallback; the terms are plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Section 16 machinery it invokes.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c132","reasoning_cat1":"'for good cause shown' is an open standard, but it is gated by a named body's consent.","reasoning_cat2":"It is the express exception to 10-G's 'Except as hereinafter provided' cap.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c133","reasoning_cat1":"'any assistance in the matter of deliveries or distribution,' 'jointly or severally, either directly or indirectly' is an unbounded prohibition with no examples.","reasoning_cat2":"It works with 16-N's exception permitting action against a non-complying party; no contradiction found.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c134","reasoning_cat1":"A short referral clause.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 16-A's grievance machinery.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c135","reasoning_cat1":"'To the extent permitted by law' and 'or is willing to enter into written collective agreement' leave both the legality and the trigger of the prohibition genuinely open.","reasoning_cat2":"17-B's separability clause provides the machinery for a provision that turns out to be unlawful, and 12-B independently deems certain wholesalers employees.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c136","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence referral.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 16-A.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c137","reasoning_cat1":"A deeming rule ('in no event shall a wholesaler ... be deemed an independent contractor if he delivers only one newspaper') immediately swallowed by 'present practices excepted, however' — the exception has no stated content.","reasoning_cat2":"Deeming such a person 'an employee of the Publisher ... subject to all of the terms and conditions hereof' has consequences for 13-H and 13-I contributions and for the 2-A.1 unit definition.","prob_cat1":0.43,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c138","reasoning_cat1":"The text is so corrupted here that the operative sentence is unreadable, and 'present practices' and 'good cause shown' are both undefined.","reasoning_cat2":"3-G states the identical rule word for word, so the instrument contains the same provision twice in two different sections.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c139","reasoning_cat1":"'it shall include only' followed by an enumerated list is a deliberate expressio unius, and the text is numerically corrupt ('within 380 days').","reasoning_cat2":"The 15-day cap on suspension and merger pay in 3(e) sits against Section 18's grant of 'eight weeks (40 shifts) pay' for the same category of loss.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c140","reasoning_cat1":"'reasonable and expeditious arrangements' and 'fully and promptly' are soft, but the clause is only a savings provision.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 12-D.1's primary/secondary payment structure.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c141","reasoning_cat1":"'shall endeavor to have said successor make the payments' is an effort obligation with no benchmark.","reasoning_cat2":"It extends 12-D.1 to cases where no Publisher acted, which is a different trigger from 12-D.1's; the two must be read together.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c142","reasoning_cat1":"The rate tables are numerically corrupted in this text (e.g. '$12,013', '$' .026'), so the figures cannot be read off the page.","reasoning_cat2":"13-A.4's cost-of-living allowance adds to 'the day scales' set here, and 13-H/13-I compute contributions from these rates.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c143","reasoning_cat1":"Beyond the corrupted figures, 'an amount of $6.00 per week per employee ... will be allocated to a fringe benefit' does not say which fringe benefit or who decides.","reasoning_cat2":"13-H.1 separately raises the additional welfare contribution to $7.00 per shift in the second year, so how the $6.00 weekly allocation interacts with the Fund contributions is unresolved.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c144","reasoning_cat1":"Again a rate table whose figures are corrupted in the printed text.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits within the same COLA and contribution architecture as 13-A.1 and 13-A.2.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c145","reasoning_cat1":"The formula is detailed, but 'multiplied by the day scales' and inclusion in 'all premiums and fringes such as pension and welfare contributions ... etc.' leave the reach of the adjustment open-ended.","reasoning_cat2":"It expressly feeds the 13-H and 13-I contribution bases and the 13-A tables, so any COLA dispute propagates through them.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c146","reasoning_cat1":"'prohibit, nullify or reduce any scheduled wage increase' is a broad trigger for a drastic remedy, and 'terminate this contract' is not limited to the wage articles.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 19 fixes the term through March 30, 1984 and 16-N bars strikes 'during the term hereof,' so a unilateral union termination right cuts across both.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c147","reasoning_cat1":"The bracket table is riddled with gaps and impossible entries as printed ('More Than 223 / Fewer Than 225 = 19'), so days falling on the boundaries have no assigned entitlement.","reasoning_cat2":"13-B.4 caps vacations at twenty days, consistent with the table's top entry; the defect is internal to the table.","prob_cat1":0.38,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c148","reasoning_cat1":"'arranged at the convenience of the employer, but on the basis of seniority' points two ways in a single sentence, and 'The spirit and purpose of this provision' invites purposive argument.","reasoning_cat2":"13-B.3 preserves 'present practices concerning the splitting of vacations' while this paragraph requires that 'the days of the vacation period shall be consecutive,' and 20-D gives the Foreman discretion over scheduling.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c149","reasoning_cat1":"'in addition to the maximum vacation pay that he would have received had he worked the full year' is a counterfactual measure that could be read as twenty days regardless of actual service.","reasoning_cat2":"13-B.4 says 'in no case ... shall an employee receive more than twenty (20) days' vacation in a calendar year,' which is hard to reconcile with paying accrued credits plus a full maximum year.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c150","reasoning_cat1":"One sentence preserving unidentified 'present practices' — the entire content is outside the document.","reasoning_cat2":"13-B.2(a) requires that 'the days of the vacation period shall be consecutive,' which is the opposite of splitting vacations.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c151","reasoning_cat1":"The twenty-day cap and the holiday carve-out are clear, though 'in any one office' hints at multi-office accrual questions.","reasoning_cat2":"13-B.2(b)'s death benefit and 20-D's Group 1 holiday rule both key off this paragraph and pull against its cap.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c152","reasoning_cat1":"A precise year-by-year effective-date schedule.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 19's term and 13-B.1's prior-calendar-year basis.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c153","reasoning_cat1":"A narrow crediting rule with two express provisos.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 13-B.2(a)'s anti-duplication principle.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c154","reasoning_cat1":"'any work lying outside the operations set forth in Section 2 hereof performed under the jurisdiction of a foreman' defines a residual category by two overlapping tests and pegs its pay to routemen.","reasoning_cat2":"2-K bars employees in non-covered capacities from performing Section 2 operations, and 20-B commissions a study 'to define the types of clerical work which are appropriate to the deliverer's bargaining unit' — the boundary is admittedly unsettled.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c155","reasoning_cat1":"'All overtime shall be compensated at a rate of one and a half times the regular hourly rate' is unqualified on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"5-H, 5-I and 7-E each require 'double the ... overtime rates' in specified circumstances, and 7-B requires time and a half of the holiday rate — direct rate conflicts with the word 'All.'","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c156","reasoning_cat1":"The text is badly broken ('Employees engaged in the net of any of the operations ... foF isher') and the ratio formula it states is opaque even when reconstructed.","reasoning_cat2":"13-E.2 permits the Publisher to modify or abrogate such excess-rate agreements at will, which largely undoes the guarantee here.","prob_cat1":0.46,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c157","reasoning_cat1":"The paragraph is physically scrambled with 13-F in this printing, and its operative words ('subject at all times to the control of the Publisher ... may at any time be modified or abrogated') are one-sided and open.","reasoning_cat2":"13-E.1 promises that over-scale employees 'shall ... receive compensation at a rate which shall have the same relation to the regular rate,' a promise this paragraph lets the Publisher revoke unilaterally.","prob_cat1":0.44,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c158","reasoning_cat1":"The printed text is interleaved with 13-E.2, but the substantive option and the two days' pay are clear.","reasoning_cat2":"It carves out Publishers 'now billing through the auditing department,' matching the same carve-out in 2-A.1's 'Collectors' entry.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c159","reasoning_cat1":"'excessive or repeated shortages' is a vague trigger and 'such relief as it may deem proper' an open remedy, though the percentage cap is precise.","reasoning_cat2":"It routes to the Section 16 machinery consistently with the rest of the Agreement.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c160","reasoning_cat1":"The contribution percentage is corrupted ('644%'), and 'each employee's rate per shift' is not the same phrase as 13-I.1's 'pay rate per shift,' leaving the base arguable.","reasoning_cat2":"13-K.3 adds paid-leave days to the days for which contributions are made, 13-A.4 folds COLA into the base, and 13-A.2 allocates $6.00 per week to an unspecified fringe — several provisions bear on the same contribution calculation.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c161","reasoning_cat1":"A short cost-shifting rule tied to a fixed 30¢ threshold.","reasoning_cat2":"It fits within the Welfare Fund scheme of 13-H.1; no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c162","reasoning_cat1":"'the term \"employee\" shall include any individual whose retirement was recognized by the Trustees subsequent to any date on which his employer commenced the payment of contributions in his behalf' is circular and its practical reach cannot be stated with confidence.","reasoning_cat2":"13-H.1 fixes contributions by reference to 'each employee in the bargaining unit,' a different and narrower population than this definition describes.","prob_cat1":0.45,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c163","reasoning_cat1":"'other employers of individuals working under provisions substantially the same as those of this Agreement' is a vague eligibility test for participation.","reasoning_cat2":"13-I.2 states a near-identical rule for the Pension Fund but adds 'to the extent that the Trust Agreement may so provide,' a qualifier missing here.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c164","reasoning_cat1":"'8% of each employee's pay rate per shift for each shift worked by each employee in the bargaining unit' leaves 'pay rate per shift' and the unit membership test to do heavy lifting, and the five-shift cap is per office.","reasoning_cat2":"13-K.3 requires contributions on paid-leave days not worked, 13-A.4 folds COLA into the base, and 22-D(vi) gives benefit credits for a fifth shift not actually worked — all of which qualify 'each shift worked.'","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.35},
{"clause_id":"c165","reasoning_cat1":"'other employers of individuals working under provisions substantially the same as those as set forth herein' is vague, and the sentence has a doubled 'as those as.'","reasoning_cat2":"It differs from the parallel Welfare Fund clause 13-H.4 by subordinating union payments to the Trust Agreement, a difference that could matter.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c166","reasoning_cat1":"'at least six (6) months of priority in the shop' uses 'priority' in a sense that 4-A.1(b) defines as a promotion order rather than a period of time.","reasoning_cat2":"The eligibility conditions (24-hour written notice, court clerk's statement) are self-contained; no competing provision found.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c167","reasoning_cat1":"The bracket table overlaps and gaps as printed ('More Than 33 / Fewer Than 76' then 'More Than 75 / Fewer Than 118'), so 75 and 76 days fall in two brackets or none.","reasoning_cat2":"'days to be counted as provided in Section 13-B' imports the vacation-credit rules, which are themselves intricate.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c168","reasoning_cat1":"'shall not be taken in such a manner as to interfere with adequate staffing' is a vague limit on an otherwise unconditional right to take accumulated leave, and '80 days' is a misprint.","reasoning_cat2":"20-A prescribes a different measure for paying unused leave ('normal straight-time weekly pay' / 'the rate he receives for the majority of his shifts') than this paragraph's 'then prevailing rate.'","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.37},
{"clause_id":"c169","reasoning_cat1":"Dense but determinate: paid-leave days count as days worked for vacation, leave and fund contributions.","reasoning_cat2":"It expands the contribution base beyond 13-H.1 and 13-I.1's 'each shift worked,' so the two must be harmonised.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.26},

{"clause_id":"c197","reasoning_cat1":"A simple equal cost-sharing rule.","reasoning_cat2":"It allocates costs to 'the Publishers' Association' although Section 19 treats the contract as individual agreements with each Publisher.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.23},

{"clause_id":"c199","reasoning_cat1":"The italicised text is garbled beyond reading ('such men to be comtion for which they are required') and is simultaneously declared 'for reference only and not as a part of this Agreement.'","reasoning_cat2":"The reprinted 'old 2-L' contains the fifth-shift overtime sentence that is operative today as 2-L.3, so the same words appear both inside and outside the Agreement, and 17-A.2 can revive them.","prob_cat1":0.47,"prob_cat2":0.49},
{"clause_id":"c200","reasoning_cat1":"'if any provision ... no longer is held to be inoperative' is a double negative that states the opposite of what is evidently meant, and 'court of highest resource' is a misprint for 'resort.'","reasoning_cat2":"Automatic revival of the closed-shop language collides with 2-L.1's commitment to 'the maximum Union security permissible under the Labor Management Relations Act' and with 17-B's requirement of agreement or an Appeals Board determination before a provision changes status.","prob_cat1":0.54,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c201","reasoning_cat1":"Long but carefully sequenced: conflict, inoperativeness, survival of the remainder, renegotiation, referral.","reasoning_cat2":"17-A.2 makes revival of excluded provisions automatic without any of these steps, and 4-A.5 supplies a separate conformity mechanism for hiring practices.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c202","reasoning_cat1":"'the spirit as well as the letter of this Agreement is to be observed in full' invokes an unstated standard, and 'renders impossible or inoperative any provisions' is broad.","reasoning_cat2":"21-D VIII says the Newspoint agreement 'supersedes and replaces all other agreements, memoranda or practices,' while the closing memorandum continues 'every memorandum, letter agreement or side agreement' — both sit awkwardly with a promise not to enter agreements that render provisions inoperative.","prob_cat1":0.35,"prob_cat2":0.28},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c113","reasoning_cat1":"'from the beginning of the night shift on the night before the holiday to the end of the day shift of the holiday itself' is a workable but unusual span definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Because 5-B's night shift runs to 10:00 a.m. and 5-A's day shift to 8:00 p.m., the holiday span overlaps two calendar days and must be reconciled with 7-C and 7-E.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c114","reasoning_cat1":"'thereafter price and one-half of the holiday rate' is a plain misprint for 'time and one-half,' and the two-days'-pay floor plus premium structure is hard to read as written.","reasoning_cat2":"It cross-refers to 'sick leave as defined in Section 18-B. 2.' when the sick-leave definition is in 13-B.2, and 7-E sets a different (double-rate) formula for holiday work at a non-issuing Publisher.","prob_cat1":0.42,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c115","reasoning_cat1":"The qualifying test ('at least four (4) days' work ... during each of the three (3) payroll weeks immediately preceding ... and during such week as well') is arithmetically precise.","reasoning_cat2":"20-D applies this test to Group 1 men on vacation while directing payment 'in accordance with Section 13-B. 4,' knitting three provisions together in a way that needs reconciling.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c116","reasoning_cat1":"'double the regular and overtime rates' is a clear formula on its own.","reasoning_cat2":"7-C prescribes 'not less than two (2) days' pay for the regular shift worked and thereafter [time] and one-half of the holiday rate' for the same act of working a holiday, so the two premium formulas overlap.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.37},
{"clause_id":"c117","reasoning_cat1":"An anti-offset rule stated plainly with defined statutory references.","reasoning_cat2":"It parallels 22-F and 22-G's anti-reduction promises; no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c118","reasoning_cat1":"'provided these activities do not interfere with the performance of their duties' is a vague proviso, though the following sentence narrows it.","reasoning_cat2":"8-C reinforces the same protection for overtime distribution; no contrary provision found.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c119","reasoning_cat1":"The 48-hour overtime production duty and the three-week look-back are precise, though the unrelated final sentence about chapel meetings sits oddly.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 20-F's paycheck-error correction and 5-J's list of starting times; no conflict located.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c120","reasoning_cat1":"'will not be discriminated against insofar as the distribution of overtime' is grammatically incomplete but its sense is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"It qualifies 5-M's employer control over overtime distribution without contradicting it.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c121","reasoning_cat1":"A mandatory routing rule ('shall be delivered in bulk from the place of printing to the plant or plants operated by the Publisher') whose scope turns on 'not owned or controlled,' an undefined test.","reasoning_cat2":"9-B softens the same subject to an 'endeavor' qualified by cost and jurisdictional escape, and the Lancaster side letter treats outside-plant transport as still to be negotiated.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c122","reasoning_cat1":"'shall endeavor' plus 'providing doing so does not involve the Publisher in increased cost or a jurisdictional conflict' makes the obligation nearly self-cancelling and supplies no cost benchmark.","reasoning_cat2":"9-A states the delivery requirement in mandatory terms for the same category of outside-printed sections, so the two paragraphs impose different levels of obligation.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c123","reasoning_cat1":"'upon such terms as may be agreed upon between such boys and the Publishers' leaves the entire employment relationship outside the Agreement's terms.","reasoning_cat2":"2-A.1 recognises the Union as exclusive representative for the listed operations and 2-K bars non-covered employees from performing them, which is difficult to square with individually negotiated non-member helpers.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c124","reasoning_cat1":"'working within the hours hereinafter specified in aid of and under the direction of a route man' is a definition that depends entirely on 10-D.","reasoning_cat2":"2-M says 'No employee shall engage any person to aid him in the performance of the work assigned to him,' which reads awkwardly against a category defined as aiding a routeman.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c125","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line categorical prohibition.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 10-D's limitation to afternoon papers.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c126","reasoning_cat1":"'between the hours of three o'clock and eight o'clock in the afternoon' is loosely expressed (eight o'clock is not afternoon) but the intended window is evident.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 10-C and 10-B's 'hours hereinafter specified.'","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.11},

{"clause_id":"c128","reasoning_cat1":"'all such boys now in their employ' fixes a baseline at an unstated date in a document reprinting decades-old text.","reasoning_cat2":"The freeze depends on the same 'now' used in 10-G and 10-H, so the whole Section 10 baseline is undated together.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c129","reasoning_cat1":"'the number ... now employed by him' and 'on which none is being employed at this time' freeze an unidentified historical baseline, and the sentence stacks four negatives.","reasoning_cat2":"10-J allows an increase 'even though it may thereby increase the total number,' an express exception to this cap.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.18},

{"clause_id":"c132","reasoning_cat1":"'for good cause shown' is an open standard, but it is gated by a named body's consent.","reasoning_cat2":"It is the express exception to 10-G's 'Except as hereinafter provided' cap.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c133","reasoning_cat1":"'any assistance in the matter of deliveries or distribution,' 'jointly or severally, either directly or indirectly' is an unbounded prohibition with no examples.","reasoning_cat2":"It works with 16-N's exception permitting action against a non-complying party; no contradiction found.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.17},

{"clause_id":"c135","reasoning_cat1":"'To the extent permitted by law' and 'or is willing to enter into written collective agreement' leave both the legality and the trigger of the prohibition genuinely open.","reasoning_cat2":"17-B's separability clause provides the machinery for a provision that turns out to be unlawful, and 12-B independently deems certain wholesalers employees.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c136","reasoning_cat1":"A one-sentence referral.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 16-A.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c137","reasoning_cat1":"A deeming rule ('in no event shall a wholesaler ... be deemed an independent contractor if he delivers only one newspaper') immediately swallowed by 'present practices excepted, however' — the exception has no stated content.","reasoning_cat2":"Deeming such a person 'an employee of the Publisher ... subject to all of the terms and conditions hereof' has consequences for 13-H and 13-I contributions and for the 2-A.1 unit definition.","prob_cat1":0.43,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c138","reasoning_cat1":"The text is so corrupted here that the operative sentence is unreadable, and 'present practices' and 'good cause shown' are both undefined.","reasoning_cat2":"3-G states the identical rule word for word, so the instrument contains the same provision twice in two different sections.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c139","reasoning_cat1":"'it shall include only' followed by an enumerated list is a deliberate expressio unius, and the text is numerically corrupt ('within 380 days').","reasoning_cat2":"The 15-day cap on suspension and merger pay in 3(e) sits against Section 18's grant of 'eight weeks (40 shifts) pay' for the same category of loss.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c140","reasoning_cat1":"'reasonable and expeditious arrangements' and 'fully and promptly' are soft, but the clause is only a savings provision.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 12-D.1's primary/secondary payment structure.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c141","reasoning_cat1":"'shall endeavor to have said successor make the payments' is an effort obligation with no benchmark.","reasoning_cat2":"It extends 12-D.1 to cases where no Publisher acted, which is a different trigger from 12-D.1's; the two must be read together.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c142","reasoning_cat1":"The rate tables are numerically corrupted in this text (e.g. '$12,013', '$' .026'), so the figures cannot be read off the page.","reasoning_cat2":"13-A.4's cost-of-living allowance adds to 'the day scales' set here, and 13-H/13-I compute contributions from these rates.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c143","reasoning_cat1":"Beyond the corrupted figures, 'an amount of $6.00 per week per employee ... will be allocated to a fringe benefit' does not say which fringe benefit or who decides.","reasoning_cat2":"13-H.1 separately raises the additional welfare contribution to $7.00 per shift in the second year, so how the $6.00 weekly allocation interacts with the Fund contributions is unresolved.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.30},

{"clause_id":"c145","reasoning_cat1":"The formula is detailed, but 'multiplied by the day scales' and inclusion in 'all premiums and fringes such as pension and welfare contributions ... etc.' leave the reach of the adjustment open-ended.","reasoning_cat2":"It expressly feeds the 13-H and 13-I contribution bases and the 13-A tables, so any COLA dispute propagates through them.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c146","reasoning_cat1":"'prohibit, nullify or reduce any scheduled wage increase' is a broad trigger for a drastic remedy, and 'terminate this contract' is not limited to the wage articles.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 19 fixes the term through March 30, 1984 and 16-N bars strikes 'during the term hereof,' so a unilateral union termination right cuts across both.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.42},
