{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c207","reasoning_cat1":"'is in the hope that the parties may arrive at an agreement' states an aspiration, not an obligation, so it is unclear whether anything is promised.","reasoning_cat2":"It is an explanatory recital sitting directly beneath the operative notice rule in 19(a), and it references a sixty-five-day period that appears nowhere else in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c208","reasoning_cat1":"The paragraph gives two different measures for the same payment — 'pay at his normal straight-time weekly pay' and 'the rate he receives for the majority of his shifts' — and weekly pay for daily leave makes little sense as written.","reasoning_cat2":"13-K.2 provides that unused accumulated leave is 'paid at the then prevailing rate,' a third measure for the same entitlement.","prob_cat1":0.43,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c209","reasoning_cat1":"'clerical work which are appropriate to the deliverer's bargaining unit' is an undefined category, and the clause promises only a study, not a result.","reasoning_cat2":"It concedes that the boundary set by 2-A.1, 2-B and 13-C is unsettled, which is exactly the kind of admission that fuels jurisdictional disputes.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c210","reasoning_cat1":"'overtime which would normally be assigned to employees who are paid a higher rate' turns on 'normally,' with no baseline stated.","reasoning_cat2":"5-M gives the employer the right to require overtime and routes unfairness charges to the Joint Standing Committee, so the two overtime rules must be read together.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c211","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence stacks a parenthetical ('discounting the vacation period before or after the holiday') on two cross-references and then adds an unrelated proviso about the Foreman's scheduling option.","reasoning_cat2":"It sends the reader to 13-B.4 for holiday pay although 7-D is the extras' holiday provision, and its grant of Foreman discretion cuts against 13-B.2(a)'s 'convenience of the employer, but on the basis of seniority.'","prob_cat1":0.39,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c212","reasoning_cat1":"'Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in the Agreement' is a blanket override whose reach is not delimited.","reasoning_cat2":"By its terms it displaces Sections 3, 4, 5 and 16 for any Bulldog elimination, and 20-E.6 expressly disapplies 'the provisions of Sections 3 and 4' to a subset of employees.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.41},
{"clause_id":"c213","reasoning_cat1":"A bare written-notice duty with no timing requirement, which is a small gap but a real one.","reasoning_cat2":"The closing memorandum requiring thirty days' notice of 'any major change in its operations which has an impact on a significant number of its NMDU employees' plausibly covers the same event with a deadline.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c214","reasoning_cat1":"'will not be laid off because of its elimination ... but will be declared to be an \"excess situation holder\"' is clear, though it depends on the Publisher's designation under 20-E.4.","reasoning_cat2":"20-E.6 carves out excess situation holders aged seventy or more from this protection, and 3-D.1 preserves a general layoff right for economic reasons.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c215","reasoning_cat1":"'no longer required because of such elimination' is a causal test applied unilaterally by the party with the interest in the answer.","reasoning_cat2":"3-D.5 uses a comparable but differently worded 'excess of regular situations' determination with a two-week deadline, which this paragraph omits.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c216","reasoning_cat1":"'When a vacant situation is to be filled or a new situation created it shall be filled by an \"excess situation holder\"' is mandatory and clear.","reasoning_cat2":"4-B requires four weeks' posting and permanent filling by seniority among regular situation holders, and 4-A.2(c) sets a group order — this paragraph overrides both without saying so.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c217","reasoning_cat1":"'other available work described in Section 2 of the Agreement for which they are qualified' is bounded by an identifiable list.","reasoning_cat2":"It preserves regular-situation-holder rates and conditions, consistent with 13-A and 13-C.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c218","reasoning_cat1":"The final clause is grammatically broken — 'except as to \"excess situation holders\" who are seventy (70) or more years of age nor shall the provisions of Sections 3 and 4 ... be applicable to them' — so it is unclear whether the age group loses layoff protection, loses Sections 3 and 4, or both.","reasoning_cat2":"Disapplying 'Sections 3 and 4' to a class of employees strips them of the seniority, layoff-notice and automation protections that the rest of the Agreement makes central.","prob_cat1":0.50,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c219","reasoning_cat1":"'at the discretion of the Publishers and may be done in a manner calculated to minimize the hiring of extras' is a broad and one-sided grant.","reasoning_cat2":"5-J requires four days' notice of any change in starting time or days off, 16-M.3 requires consent for changes in condition, and the Times Supplementary Agreement ¶4 guarantees named holders against starting-time changes.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.43},
{"clause_id":"c220","reasoning_cat1":"The News obligation is precisely timed, but 'The Times will continue its present practice' states no standard at all.","reasoning_cat2":"The same asymmetric device appears in the vacation-check letters, so the pattern is consistent even if individually empty.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c221","reasoning_cat1":"The clause is circular — questions 'which are subject to arbitration under the contract and which are submitted to arbitration will be arbitrated under Section 16' — and so decides nothing.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 16 already covers all disputes 'arising out of the interpretation or application of this Agreement,' making this either redundant or an implied narrowing.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c222","reasoning_cat1":"'on its own present press equipment' and 'what are currently known as' peg the obligation to an unstated moment, and the section names differ by borough in a way that must be traced.","reasoning_cat2":"21-B.4 declares that 'this agreement [concerning all-advertising sections] ends effective March 30, 1975,' so whether this paragraph is operative in a 1981-84 contract is genuinely open.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c223","reasoning_cat1":"The three named holidays and the Section 3 condition are specific and applicable.","reasoning_cat2":"Like 21-B.1 it is expressly terminated by 21-B.4 as of March 30, 1975, yet is reprinted as operative text in a 1981 agreement.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c224","reasoning_cat1":"The alternating quarters are precisely described, but every date runs from 1974 to March 1975 and is wholly spent.","reasoning_cat2":"Reproducing an expired limitation in a 1981-84 agreement, alongside the closing memorandum that continues every side agreement 'deemed updated,' leaves its status unresolvable.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.47},
{"clause_id":"c225","reasoning_cat1":"A single dated termination sentence; its own words are unambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"It says the all-advertising agreement ended in March 1975, yet it and 21-B.1 to 21-B.3 are printed as operative provisions of a contract running to March 1984, and the closing memorandum continues every memorandum 'deemed updated.'","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.54},
{"clause_id":"c226","reasoning_cat1":"'when the regular roto is 75, 60, 50, 40 or fewer copies per load' enumerates values and then adds 'or fewer,' and the benefit runs to four named individuals only.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits in a section of shop-specific memoranda and does not conflict with the general overtime rules of 5-F and 13-D.","prob_cat1":0.35,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c227","reasoning_cat1":"'At 148 or more pages per copy ... no more than 240 loads' is fully specified with a stated exception for pallet trucks.","reasoning_cat2":"21-D I and 21-C.3(g) set different load and tailman thresholds for News operations, and 3-A.2 requires plant schedules — several caps govern the same trucks.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c228","reasoning_cat1":"The eight lettered items mix hard rules with a promise to 'send letter that it will meet,' and 'There are now 133 a.m. routes' fixes a baseline at an undated moment.","reasoning_cat2":"Item (g) expressly yields to 'the Newspoint Agreement' for tailman thresholds, while 21-D I sets different tailman schedules — the two must be sequenced.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c229","reasoning_cat1":"'Bindery Operation — Transport men hired according to need' is a fragment with no verb, no obligor and no standard for 'need' — the kind of shorthand that has to be construed to mean anything.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits against 4-A.2's mandatory group hiring order and 21-D III's fixed manning table, both of which constrain hiring 'according to need.'","prob_cat1":0.50,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c230","reasoning_cat1":"The table is internally corrupt (the '45 papers' row falls between 100 and 50, dealer counts include '$0'), and the closing sentence — 'Tailmen will be employed on all runs covered by this Schedule \"A\"' — contradicts a column headed 'Maximum Number of Loads with[out] Tailmen.'","reasoning_cat2":"Schedules B and C provide 'Without a Tailman' maxima with a footnote that Schedule A applies if exceeded, so the tailman trigger works differently in each schedule.","prob_cat1":0.48,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c231","reasoning_cat1":"The asterisk in the column heading has no footnote attached to this schedule, leaving the escape condition unstated on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"The footnote appears only under Schedule C ('If these schedules are exceeded then Schedule \"A\" will apply'), so whether it governs Schedule B too is genuinely open.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c232","reasoning_cat1":"'If these schedules are exceeded then Schedule \"A\" will apply' is a clear fallback, though 'these schedules' is plural and may reach beyond Schedule C.","reasoning_cat2":"Schedule A itself requires tailmen on all covered runs, so triggering it converts a 'without a tailman' limit into a with-tailman regime.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c233","reasoning_cat1":"The parenthetical definition of recovery runs and the 100-load ceiling are both precise.","reasoning_cat2":"Schedule A excludes recovery runs from its tailman requirement, consistent with this paragraph's conditional approach.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c234","reasoning_cat1":"'Present practice with respect to running time' incorporates an unstated and unidentified practice.","reasoning_cat2":"22-D(ix) sets a numerical run-time rule for The Times, showing that the parties knew how to specify running time when they wished to.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c235","reasoning_cat1":"A flat numerical maximum with a clear condition.","reasoning_cat2":"21-C.2 caps News trucks at 240 loads in different circumstances; the two caps govern different runs.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c236","reasoning_cat1":"'present practice will be continued' supplies no content whatever for pallet-truck loading.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits directly beside the precise 250-load rule in II.A, an asymmetry that invites argument about what the practice is.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c237","reasoning_cat1":"'(Day side, double out only)' uses undefined jargon, and item (c) — floormen 'to be used when and where needed as directed' — has no fixed content.","reasoning_cat2":"The Times Supplementary Agreement fixes floor manning numerically at the other plants, showing a different drafting approach to the same subject.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c238","reasoning_cat1":"The text is corrupted ('two 15 minute coffee breaks (one in the [morning] and one in the afternoon) shall be [provided]'), and 'if the requirements of the operation necessitate it' is an open escape.","reasoning_cat2":"5-N sets the general paid-lunch rule and 22-A gives Carlstadt floormen 40 minutes with different coffee breaks, so three different lunch regimes coexist.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c239","reasoning_cat1":"'the contractually designated \"territorial coverage\"' points to Section 1's 'approximately' drawn boundary, and 'in line with current policy' is unbounded.","reasoning_cat2":"Item (c) disapplies 'the \"extra crew\" requirements of Section 8-L' when the extra-crew rule is in Section 3-L — a mis-citation of the provision being overridden.","prob_cat1":0.43,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c240","reasoning_cat1":"The paragraph promises the 58 men 'will continue to be employed on the day side' and then says it is not 'a guaranty of 58 day jobs' — the promise and the disclaimer are hard to hold together.","reasoning_cat2":"It also preserves the Union's right to argue that vacated jobs stay on the day side, so the same sentence leaves the underlying question expressly unresolved.","prob_cat1":0.48,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c241","reasoning_cat1":"A short posting requirement referring to a specific section.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4-B's posting and bidding rules.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c242","reasoning_cat1":"'supersedes and replaces all other agreements, memoranda or practices which would otherwise relate or be applicable to the Newspoint operation except as otherwise stated herein' is a broad supersession with a self-referential exception.","reasoning_cat2":"The closing memorandum says 'Every memorandum, letter agreement or side agreement shall be continued through the term of this agreement and deemed updated,' and 21-C.3(g) defers to 'the Newspoint Agreement' — the priority order is genuinely contested.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.48},
{"clause_id":"c243","reasoning_cat1":"'The IBM stipulation continues as it applies to the Daily News only' incorporates an unidentified document, and 'reviewed and revised in a fair and equitable manner' states no standard.","reasoning_cat2":"The franchise-exclusivity sentence repeats 21-C.3(e), and the one-week notice of delivery-method changes overlaps 5-J and 16-M.3.","prob_cat1":0.47,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c244","reasoning_cat1":"The actuarial mechanism is carefully specified, but it is directed at 'the calendar year 1966' with no updating language.","reasoning_cat2":"Reproduced in a 1981-84 agreement whose own pension provisions are 13-I and whose closing memorandum deems side agreements 'updated,' its present operation is unclear.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c245","reasoning_cat1":"'The Union shall select one option' is written as if the choice were still to be made, with no deadline and no default.","reasoning_cat2":"Paragraph 1 makes the News's contribution turn on 'the plan as selected in paragraph 2,' so an unexercised option leaves the funding obligation indeterminate.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c246","reasoning_cat1":"The anti-offset promise is precise, but the change-control condition requires 'advance written approval of the chapel and advance written approval of the Union' without saying what happens if they differ.","reasoning_cat2":"22-F states the same anti-offset principle for The Times without any approval requirement, and 21-F.2(b) presents an alternative that would replace this plan entirely.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.35},
{"clause_id":"c247","reasoning_cat1":"'benefits shall be provided under a new pension plan, the terms of which shall be jointly agreed upon' is a bare agreement to agree with no fallback.","reasoning_cat2":"Paragraph 1's actuarial arbitration is directed at cost, not terms, so a failure to agree the plan terms has no resolution route.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c248","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence has lost its structure ('In the event that it is mutually agreed that a pension agreement already negotiated ... or there is a pension agreement which is negotiated during past or current negotiations'), and 'taken in their entirety, are more favorable' is an unbounded comparison.","reasoning_cat2":"The October 7, 1981 letter contains a differently worded most-favoured-nation promise on 'pension, welfare and insurance benefits' with productivity and pattern-package carve-outs that do not appear here.","prob_cat1":0.47,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c249","reasoning_cat1":"'the parties acknowledged the need for The News to operate as efficiently as possible' and 'would have a significant impact on the deliverers' are statements of view, not obligations.","reasoning_cat2":"This recital of efficiency pulls in the opposite direction from the operative veto in 21-G.2 ('shall not be put into effect without agreement of the NMDU'), a classic recital-versus-operative tension.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c250","reasoning_cat1":"'Such concept shall not be put into effect without agreement of the NMDU' is an unambiguous veto.","reasoning_cat2":"It cuts across 3-B and 3-D.1's unilateral rights to rearrange routes and deliveries, and the preceding recital in 21-G.1 recognises the need for efficiency.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c251","reasoning_cat1":"'will expire in three years [from March 31, 1981]' relies on bracketed editorial matter to be intelligible at all.","reasoning_cat2":"Three years from March 31, 1981 is March 31, 1984, one day after Section 19's expiry date of March 30, 1984.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c252","reasoning_cat1":"'commit themselves to the achievement of maximum productivity and efficiency ... consistent with the terms of this memorandum and of the contract' is an aspiration immediately qualified by a saving for Union manning demands.","reasoning_cat2":"The recital about the Carlstadt capital investment and productivity gains points against the detailed manning and jurisdiction guarantees that follow it and against 21-G-style union vetoes elsewhere.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.44},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c207","reasoning_cat1":"'is in the hope that the parties may arrive at an agreement' states an aspiration, not an obligation, so it is unclear whether anything is promised.","reasoning_cat2":"It is an explanatory recital sitting directly beneath the operative notice rule in 19(a), and it references a sixty-five-day period that appears nowhere else in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c208","reasoning_cat1":"The paragraph gives two different measures for the same payment — 'pay at his normal straight-time weekly pay' and 'the rate he receives for the majority of his shifts' — and weekly pay for daily leave makes little sense as written.","reasoning_cat2":"13-K.2 provides that unused accumulated leave is 'paid at the then prevailing rate,' a third measure for the same entitlement.","prob_cat1":0.43,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c209","reasoning_cat1":"'clerical work which are appropriate to the deliverer's bargaining unit' is an undefined category, and the clause promises only a study, not a result.","reasoning_cat2":"It concedes that the boundary set by 2-A.1, 2-B and 13-C is unsettled, which is exactly the kind of admission that fuels jurisdictional disputes.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c210","reasoning_cat1":"'overtime which would normally be assigned to employees who are paid a higher rate' turns on 'normally,' with no baseline stated.","reasoning_cat2":"5-M gives the employer the right to require overtime and routes unfairness charges to the Joint Standing Committee, so the two overtime rules must be read together.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c211","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence stacks a parenthetical ('discounting the vacation period before or after the holiday') on two cross-references and then adds an unrelated proviso about the Foreman's scheduling option.","reasoning_cat2":"It sends the reader to 13-B.4 for holiday pay although 7-D is the extras' holiday provision, and its grant of Foreman discretion cuts against 13-B.2(a)'s 'convenience of the employer, but on the basis of seniority.'","prob_cat1":0.39,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c212","reasoning_cat1":"'Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary in the Agreement' is a blanket override whose reach is not delimited.","reasoning_cat2":"By its terms it displaces Sections 3, 4, 5 and 16 for any Bulldog elimination, and 20-E.6 expressly disapplies 'the provisions of Sections 3 and 4' to a subset of employees.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.41},
{"clause_id":"c213","reasoning_cat1":"A bare written-notice duty with no timing requirement, which is a small gap but a real one.","reasoning_cat2":"The closing memorandum requiring thirty days' notice of 'any major change in its operations which has an impact on a significant number of its NMDU employees' plausibly covers the same event with a deadline.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c214","reasoning_cat1":"'will not be laid off because of its elimination ... but will be declared to be an \"excess situation holder\"' is clear, though it depends on the Publisher's designation under 20-E.4.","reasoning_cat2":"20-E.6 carves out excess situation holders aged seventy or more from this protection, and 3-D.1 preserves a general layoff right for economic reasons.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c215","reasoning_cat1":"'no longer required because of such elimination' is a causal test applied unilaterally by the party with the interest in the answer.","reasoning_cat2":"3-D.5 uses a comparable but differently worded 'excess of regular situations' determination with a two-week deadline, which this paragraph omits.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c216","reasoning_cat1":"'When a vacant situation is to be filled or a new situation created it shall be filled by an \"excess situation holder\"' is mandatory and clear.","reasoning_cat2":"4-B requires four weeks' posting and permanent filling by seniority among regular situation holders, and 4-A.2(c) sets a group order — this paragraph overrides both without saying so.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c217","reasoning_cat1":"'other available work described in Section 2 of the Agreement for which they are qualified' is bounded by an identifiable list.","reasoning_cat2":"It preserves regular-situation-holder rates and conditions, consistent with 13-A and 13-C.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c218","reasoning_cat1":"The final clause is grammatically broken — 'except as to \"excess situation holders\" who are seventy (70) or more years of age nor shall the provisions of Sections 3 and 4 ... be applicable to them' — so it is unclear whether the age group loses layoff protection, loses Sections 3 and 4, or both.","reasoning_cat2":"Disapplying 'Sections 3 and 4' to a class of employees strips them of the seniority, layoff-notice and automation protections that the rest of the Agreement makes central.","prob_cat1":0.50,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c219","reasoning_cat1":"'at the discretion of the Publishers and may be done in a manner calculated to minimize the hiring of extras' is a broad and one-sided grant.","reasoning_cat2":"5-J requires four days' notice of any change in starting time or days off, 16-M.3 requires consent for changes in condition, and the Times Supplementary Agreement ¶4 guarantees named holders against starting-time changes.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.43},
{"clause_id":"c220","reasoning_cat1":"The News obligation is precisely timed, but 'The Times will continue its present practice' states no standard at all.","reasoning_cat2":"The same asymmetric device appears in the vacation-check letters, so the pattern is consistent even if individually empty.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c221","reasoning_cat1":"The clause is circular — questions 'which are subject to arbitration under the contract and which are submitted to arbitration will be arbitrated under Section 16' — and so decides nothing.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 16 already covers all disputes 'arising out of the interpretation or application of this Agreement,' making this either redundant or an implied narrowing.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c222","reasoning_cat1":"'on its own present press equipment' and 'what are currently known as' peg the obligation to an unstated moment, and the section names differ by borough in a way that must be traced.","reasoning_cat2":"21-B.4 declares that 'this agreement [concerning all-advertising sections] ends effective March 30, 1975,' so whether this paragraph is operative in a 1981-84 contract is genuinely open.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.34},

{"clause_id":"c225","reasoning_cat1":"A single dated termination sentence; its own words are unambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"It says the all-advertising agreement ended in March 1975, yet it and 21-B.1 to 21-B.3 are printed as operative provisions of a contract running to March 1984, and the closing memorandum continues every memorandum 'deemed updated.'","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.54},
{"clause_id":"c226","reasoning_cat1":"'when the regular roto is 75, 60, 50, 40 or fewer copies per load' enumerates values and then adds 'or fewer,' and the benefit runs to four named individuals only.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits in a section of shop-specific memoranda and does not conflict with the general overtime rules of 5-F and 13-D.","prob_cat1":0.35,"prob_cat2":0.20},

{"clause_id":"c228","reasoning_cat1":"The eight lettered items mix hard rules with a promise to 'send letter that it will meet,' and 'There are now 133 a.m. routes' fixes a baseline at an undated moment.","reasoning_cat2":"Item (g) expressly yields to 'the Newspoint Agreement' for tailman thresholds, while 21-D I sets different tailman schedules — the two must be sequenced.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.40},
